title: Soil organic carbon and soil biological function
mechanism: Soil organic matter contributes to aggregation, nutrient cycling and biological activity and can improve water-related soil functions.
intervention: Organic matter inputs and cover crops
evidence: FAO soil management guidance describes organic matter as central to soil structure, biological activity and water-related functions.

title: Cover crops and soil protection
mechanism: Living and residue cover protects the soil surface, adds biomass and can support aggregation and infiltration.
evidence: FAO sustainable soil management literature supports maintaining soil cover and organic inputs as core soil-management practices.

title: Agroforestry and biodiversity
mechanism: Trees and shrubs add vertical habitat structure, litter and root biomass and can diversify farm habitats.
evidence: FAO agroforestry resources describe ecological, soil and habitat functions of integrating trees with agricultural systems.

title: Habitat connectivity and fragmentation
mechanism: Land-use change and fragmentation alter habitat amount, configuration and connectivity, affecting ecological processes and species persistence.
intervention: Habitat corridors and connected native vegetation
evidence: IPCC assessments identify land-use change and habitat loss/fragmentation as major pressures on terrestrial biodiversity.

title: Climate change, drought and ecosystems
mechanism: Increasing heat and shifts in precipitation can increase water stress and alter ecosystem structure and species distributions.
intervention: Water-retaining land management and climate-resilient habitat
evidence: IPCC assessments document climate-related risks to terrestrial ecosystems from heat and water stress.

title: Pollution as a biodiversity pressure
mechanism: Pollution is a direct anthropogenic pressure that can degrade habitat and affect organisms and ecological processes.
evidence: IPBES global assessment identifies pollution among major direct drivers of biodiversity loss.

title: Habitat diversity and pollinators
mechanism: Diverse vegetation and floral resources can provide food, nesting and refuge resources for beneficial insects.
intervention: Native flowering strips and field margins
evidence: FAO biodiversity and pollination resources describe the role of diverse agricultural habitats in supporting pollinators.

title: Soil pH and nutrient availability
mechanism: Soil pH influences nutrient availability and biological processes; extreme pH can constrain plant growth and soil organisms.
intervention: Site-specific pH management based on soil testing
evidence: FAO soil management guidance treats pH as a fundamental chemical property influencing nutrient availability and soil processes.
